newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Credit Agricole privatisation completed.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Credit Agricole privatisation completed.

text.p: Belgian bank Credit Agricole/Landbouwkrediet said on Thursday its privatisation was completed after Bacob Bank became its third shareholder.
"Since October 10 Bacob Bank is, next to Swiss Life and (farmers' syndicates) Lanbokas and Agricaisse, shareholder of Credit Agricole," it said in a statement.
The three partners now each have a 33.3 percent stake in Credit Agricole, which specialises in credits to the rural community.
It had been seeking a banking partner to assure its place in a competitive environment. Swiss Life is its shareholder from the insurance sector.

Both Swiss Life and the farmers' syndicates had a call option on the Belgian state's remaining 25.1 percent which they have exercised and sold on to Bacob together with a total 8.23 percent of their own shares.

The state's stake was held through state-owned federal holding company FPM, and to complete the privatisation deal the government had to implement a law change allowing the transfer of FPM's blocking minority.
"The Royal Decree allowing FPM to transfer its stake was published in the Belgian official journal of October 10," the Credit Agricole statement said.
"This successfully completes the first process of full privatisation in our country," it said.
At the end of 1995 Credit Agricole had total assets of 148 billion francs, 9.3 billion francs of own funds and made a net profit during the year of 717 million francs.
Bacob, one of Belgium's seven largest banks, had 1995 assets worth 1,188 billion.
